To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Europeanization of Czech pro-life movement can be observed, but it does not affect all groups equally.
Europeanization is uneven, and that it is more pronounced among certain types of actors than others, and in some aspects of the pro-life movement, and not in others.

(a) Europeanization has been uneven in the Czech prolife movement; (b) it has been more prevalent in the activities of charitable organizations than in the activities of activist groups; (c) it is more prevalent in the area of international networking, and less in the area of transnational policy advocacy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how European integration affects domestic social movements.
the question of how Europeanization affects the pro-life movement, and how the pro-life movement is affected by Europeanization.
the Europeanization of social movement organizations in the context of the pro-life movement, which we define as a process of adaptation of the Czech prolife movement to EU standards.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Europeanization of social movement is a multifaceted, complex and dynamic process that is still not fully understood.
Europeanization of social movement organizations is a complex and multifaceted process, which may not be fully understood by looking at one specific case.
“Europeanization of the Czech Republic” is not a single, uniform process, but rather, a complex of processes, some of which are related, and others not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Europeanization of pro-life groups in the Czech Republic is a complex process that is not necessarily uniform across all pro-life actors and that is not necessarily the most significant factor affecting pro-life activism in the country.
the Czech Republic has become more pro-life as a result of Europeanization.
the pro-life movement is Europeanized in some areas but not in others.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Europeanization of social movement organizations is a multifaceted process, which may be more or less pronounced depending on the type of social movement organization and the specific issue at stake.
Europeanization of social movement organizations is uneven.
the pro-life movement is not a homogenous whole, but a diverse collection of organizations, groups, and actors, and that the process of Europeanization is unevenly applied to this movement.
